title: VISp history models did not remove spectral compression for two movies from 32 mice
abstract: We tested whether recent VISp responses explain higher-area spectral compression in Allen mouse movie data. The sample had 4,419 units from 32 mice. Read-outs used 300 predictor units and 100 target units per area, separate mouse groups, and guarded time validation. Independent lag coefficients reduced mean HVA explained variance by 3.17 and 3.01 percentage points in two movies. Quadratic features gave small gains and left the residual hierarchy. A declared post-result test kept the predictor count fixed and selected a shared exponential filter. On exposure-corrected responses, past smoothing gave gains of 0.01 and 0.19 points, with draw spreads [-0.49, 0.51] and [-0.16, 0.54]. Residual hierarchy slopes were 0.331 and 0.288. Other higher areas retained prediction advantages of 6.49 and 9.08 points. Alternating seven- and eight-frame bins added a 2 Hz component with about 1.6-2.1 percent of reliable variance. Exposure correction removed most of this component and kept the spectral hierarchy. Removal of frequencies at or below 1 Hz lowered mean slopes, but paired uncertainty included no reduction. The tested models did not explain the compression. Limits include two clips, 250 ms bins, finite predictor samples, and weak movie-one prediction. Bands describe 20 overlapping mouse-half draws; they are not independent confidence intervals. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included. External data remain outside the baseline bundle.
